privacy.title: Privacy — WODBurner
privacy.description: What stays on the device, what a scan sends, and how to erase it.

p: The site is published by Thomas Lloancy. For a question about these pages or your data: thomaslloancy@gmail.com.
WODBurner does not create an account. There is no password, no advertising, and no cookie set by these pages. Cloudflare, which hosts the site, can count visits.

Workouts, results, sound and volume are stored in this browser (IndexedDB). The language shown is the phone’s. The JSON export copies them. If you turn on sync, a copy encrypted in your browser with a secret key we never see is kept on our Cloudflare servers, with no name or email; turning sync off deletes it. Scanning a friend’s key copies their history into yours, with their name, and writes nothing into their backup. Erase everything removes them from the device. That is the only action that stands in for deleting an account, because there is no account.

The photo leaves the device only when you start a scan. The browser shrinks it, then sends it to WODBurner’s reading service. That service forwards it to Google Gemini for the request and does not keep it. The text you review can be saved, and only on your device, if you ask for that.
A whiteboard can show names or faces. WODBurner does not keep the image.

The scan asks for a Cloudflare Turnstile check. A daily ceiling limits how many readings can run. For that ceiling the service stores a counter tied to a hash of the IP address, not a profile under your name.
